title: Using a Grill Mat for Making Easy Outdoor Grilled Halloumi
keyword: grilling halloumi on non stick mat
meta_description: Master the art of grilling halloumi on non stick mat. Learn how to get perfect marks without the mess using BBQ Grill Mats for your next cookout.
html:
There is nothing quite like the salty, squeaky texture of perfectly cooked halloumi. It is the ultimate summer grilling cheese, capable of withstanding high heat without melting into a puddle. However, if you have ever tossed those white blocks directly onto bare grates, you know the struggle. The high milk sugar content in halloumi loves to stick to metal, and if you try to pry it off too early, you lose that beautiful golden crust. That is why I am a huge advocate for grilling halloumi on non stick mat. It guarantees a perfect sear without the heartbreak of losing half your dinner to the flames.

Why Grilling Halloumi on Non Stick Mat Wins Every Time

Traditional grilling requires meticulous timing and oil management. You have to oil the grates, oil the cheese, and hope the heat distribution is even. If you are using charcoal, flare-ups are a constant threat that can singe the cheese before it cooks through. When you switch to using a barrier like the BBQ Grill Mats, you eliminate almost all of these variables. These mats are designed to sit directly on the grill grates, creating a flat, stable surface that heats up evenly.

For delicate foods like halloumi, this is a game-changer. The non-stick surface ensures that the sugars in the cheese caramelize beautifully against the heat without bonding to the metal. You still get the grill marks and the smoky flavor infusion, but you don't have to wrestle with a spatula to get the cheese off the grill. Plus, you can cut your halloumi into thinner slices without worrying about them falling through the cracks into the fire pit.

Preparing Your Cheese for the Heat

Before you even fire up the grill, you need to prep the halloumi properly. Since the mats prevent sticking, you don't need to drench the cheese in oil, but a little preparation goes a long way for flavor.

  1. Remove from packaging: Take the halloumi out of the brine and pat it dry with paper towels. Excess moisture can steam the cheese rather than grill it.
  2. Slice it right: Cut the block into slices that are roughly 1/4 to 1/2 inch thick. If they are too thick, the outside will burn before the inside heats through; too thin, and they might dry out.
  3. Add aromatics: Lightly brush the slices with olive oil and sprinkle dried oregano, chili flakes, or a squeeze of fresh lemon juice.

Step-by-Step Guide for Grilling Halloumi on Non Stick Mat

Now that your cheese is prepped, it is time to get those BBQ Grill Mats on the grate. Because these mats are thin and conductive, they heat up rapidly, so keep a close eye on your food.

First, preheat your grill to medium-high heat, around 375°F to 400°F. Once the grill is hot, place the BBQ Grill Mats flat on the grates. Give them a minute or two to come up to temperature. You do not need to oil the mats themselves, as they are inherently non-stick, but a quick wipe helps with seasoning.

Lay your halloumi slices onto the mat in a single layer, ensuring they aren't touching so air can circulate. Let them cook undisturbed for about 2 to 3 minutes. You will start to see the edges turning brown and deep golden grill lines appearing. Because the surface is non-stick, you can slide your spatula underneath gently to check the color. Once you have a good sear, flip the slices over and cook for another 2 minutes on the other side.

Flavor Pairings and Serving Suggestions

Grilling halloumi on non stick mat provides such a clean texture that it pairs well with almost anything. Since you aren't fighting carbon buildup from dirty grates, the true flavor of the cheese shines through. I love serving the grilled cheese on a bed of arugula tossed with a lemon vinaigrette. The heat from the halloumi slightly wilts the greens, which is delicious.

For a more substantial appetizer, try skewering the grilled cheese cubes with watermelon and mint. The sweetness of the watermelon cuts right through the saltiness of the halloumi. You can also slide the grilled slices into a pita with tzatziki sauce and sliced cucumbers for a quick, vegetarian-friendly gyro. Because the BBQ Grill Mats keep the cheese intact, you get perfect, restaurant-quality slices ready for stacking.

Caring for Your BBQ Grill Mats

One of the best things about using these mats is the cleanup. When you are done grilling, simply remove the mats from the grill and let them cool. You can wash them with warm soapy water and a soft sponge—avoid using abrasive scouring pads or steel wool, as they can damage the non-stick coating. They are also dishwasher safe, which makes post-cookout chores incredibly easy. Once dry, they can be rolled up or stored flat, ready for your next grilling session.

FAQ

Do grill mats affect the taste of the food?

No, as long as you are using high-quality mats like the BBQ Grill Mats, there is no chemical taste imparted to the food. In fact, they can improve the taste because they prevent flare-ups that can cause soot or acrid flavors to settle on your cheese.

Can I use these mats on any type of grill?

Yes, these mats are versatile and work on gas, charcoal, and even electric grills. They are designed to withstand high temperatures, making them suitable for almost any outdoor cooking setup.

Will I still get grill marks on my halloumi?

Absolutely. The mats are thin enough that they transfer the heat efficiently from the grates below. If you leave the cheese on long enough without moving it, you will get distinct, appetizing grill lines just like you would on an open grate.
